references.text: Jesus' command to the paralytic to stand up, take his bed, and go home – verse 25 is the immediate fulfillment of this command.
Jesus heals a man at the Pool of Bethesda and commands him to stand up, take his mat, and walk – a parallel healing where the sick man immediately obeys and carries what he had been lying on.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of the paralytic, where the man immediately stood up, took his mat, and went out in front of everyone, and they praised God.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus commands the paralytic to stand up and take his bed, and the man gets up and goes home.
The crowd saw it and was filled with awe and praised God – a parallel to the paralytic going home and praising God.
The woman who had been bent over for eighteen years was healed by Jesus and praised God – another example of immediate healing followed by praise to God.
The leper Samaritan returned and praised God with a loud voice after being healed – a similar pattern of healing and praise.
The lame man at the Beautiful Gate was healed, jumped up, walked, and praised God – a strong parallel to the paralytic's response in Luke 5:25.
Everyone praised God for what had happened to the lame man at the temple gate – the crowd's response to a miraculous healing.
David's psalm about praising the Lord who forgives all guilt and heals all diseases – a thematic parallel to the paralytic who praises God after receiving both forgiveness and healing.
